name: Adjectival Pre-head Modifier in Nominal

examples.note: Direct property attribution; Attribution of age property to men
Special case where property is relative to context; Complement set relation

constraints.description: Mod must be AdjP with head Adj
AdjP occurs in pre-head position in Nom

grounds.locator: Ch. 5 §14.2; Ch. 6, attributive versus predicative functions

projection.target: In a former president, former modifies the relation expressed by president. The president is former does not give the same reading. A pre-head adjective need not have a matching predicative use.
projection.evidence: CGEL distinguishes attributive uses and discusses adjectives restricted to particular functions.

curious.title: Describing words in front of a noun
curious.summary: An adjective phrase placed before a noun says something about it, as in old men.
curious.body:
In old men, the word old says something about the men: they are old. The describing word comes before the noun it describes.

Not every case is that direct. In other men, the property depends on the context. And in a former president, former doesn't describe the person in the way old describes men. It modifies the relation that president expresses. This dictionary notes that an adjective placed before a noun doesn't have to work in the same way after the verb be.
curious.try: Say an adjective before a noun, such as old men. Then try the adjective after is or are. Does it still say the same thing?

teacher.summary: Teaches pre-head adjective phrases in the nominal, and why attributive adjectives need not have predicative uses.
teacher.explain: A pre-head adjective phrase attributes a property to the head noun: in old men, old attributes age to the men. Other men is a special case where the property is relative to context, with a complement-set relation. The modifier must be an adjective phrase headed by an adjective, in pre-head position in the nominal. A pre-head adjective needn't have a matching predicative use: in a former president, former modifies the relation expressed by president, and the president is former doesn't give the same reading. This dictionary treats this as a specific type of pre-head modification.
teacher.terms: Attributive adjective is the traditional term for an adjective before the noun; predicative adjective is the traditional term for one after a verb such as be.

contrasts.note: Property relative to context; complement-set relation.

watch_for: A learner might think every adjective before a noun can also follow be with the same meaning.
A learner might read other in other men as describing a property of the men themselves, as old does.
teacher.activity: Students write short noun phrases with an adjective before the noun. For each, they decide whether the adjective states a plain property or depends on context, and compare answers.

child.hook: Which word tells you more about the men in old men?
child.explain: A describing word can come before a noun. In old men, the word old tells us about the men. The describing word comes first.
child.play: Pick a noun, like dog or house. Add a describing word before it. Then try a different one, and see how the picture changes.

cite: Reynolds, Brett, ed. 2026. "Adjectival Pre-head Modifier in Nominal." English Constructionary. https://brettreynolds.ca/constructionary/linguist/nom-adjp-mod-001/ (snapshot 2026-11-19, fa37529).
